title: Two Dominican Legends, One Bronx Stage: Luis Vargas and Monchy at Lehman Center
caption_instagram:
Two Dominican legends. One Bronx stage 🇩🇴 Swipe for the night →

Luis Vargas, El Rey Supremo de la Bachata, and Monchy of Monchy & Alexandra shared the bill at @lehmancenter for Bachatéame New York. Couples left their seats and danced in the aisles, and by the end the whole room was standing.

The Den was founded by a Dominican-born, Bronx-raised storyteller, so this one was personal. Our co-founder Wally (@wstudiosnj) was on the scene.

Thank you to Leah Grammatica, Alexa Downing and the whole Lehman Center team for having the Den.

Luis Vargas or Monchy? Pick one 👇 Then send this to the person you'd dance it with.

The Den attended with media access from Lehman Center.

caption_facebook:
Two Dominican legends shared one Bronx stage. Luis Vargas, known for more than 40 years as El Rey Supremo de la Bachata, and Monchy of Monchy & Alexandra played Bachatéame New York at Lehman Center for the Performing Arts on Saturday, Nov. 21.

Couples danced in the aisles, phones went up, and the room finished on its feet. For a media company founded by a Dominican-born, Bronx-raised storyteller, this one was personal. Our co-founder Osvaldo "Wally" Rodriguez was on the scene.

Thank you to Leah Grammatica, Alexa Downing and the whole Lehman Center team for having us.

Luis Vargas or Monchy? Tell us below.

The Innovators Den attended with media access from Lehman Center. #Tarima

caption_linkedin:
Bachata was once kept off the radio in its own country. On Saturday it filled Lehman Center in the Bronx.

The Innovators Den covered Bachatéame New York with Luis Vargas and Monchy. Three things stood out:

1. Catalogs outlast trends. Luis Vargas is 65, has carried the title El Rey Supremo de la Bachata for more than 40 years, and still fills a room.
2. Crossover has a history. Monchy & Alexandra were the first bachata act on Sábado Gigante, in 2001, and helped take the genre beyond the Dominican Republic.
3. Culture travels with its people. In the Bronx, the audience danced in the aisles.

Thank you to Leah Grammatica, Alexa Downing and the Lehman Center team. Our co-founder Osvaldo "Wally" Rodriguez was on the scene.

#Music #Bronx #LatinMusic #TheInnovatorsDen

cta_line: Bachata is *Dominican*. The Bronx made it *home*.

slides.label: The night
slides.text: Saturday, *Nov. 21*. *Bachatéame New York* put *Luis Vargas* and *Monchy* on one bill at *Lehman Center for the Performing Arts* in the Bronx.

slides.label: El Rey Supremo
slides.text: *Luis Vargas* is *65*. He has carried the title *El Rey Supremo de la Bachata* for more than *40 years*, and he walked out in red with his guitar.

slides.label: The catalog
slides.text: The songs that built that title: *Loco de Amor*, *Volvió el Dolor* and *Esa Mujer*.

slides.label: Monchy
slides.text: *Monchy* is half of *Monchy & Alexandra*, the first bachata act to play *Sábado Gigante*, back in *2001*.

slides.label: The duets
slides.text: *Hoja en Blanco*. *Dos Locos*. *Perdidos*, which went to *No. 1* on Billboard's tropical chart in 2004.

slides.label: The crowd
slides.text: Couples left their seats and danced bachata *in the aisles*. Phones went up. By the end the whole room was *on its feet*.

slides.label: Why it's personal
slides.text: The Den was founded by a *Dominican-born*, *Bronx-raised* storyteller. Two Dominican legends in the Bronx, with our co-founder *Wally* on the scene.

slides.label: Thank you
slides.text: Thank you to *Leah Grammatica*, *Alexa Downing* and the whole *Lehman Center* team for having the Den.
